title: How John Rush bootstrapped Mars X and acquired Unicorn Platform: acquisitions, AI and UX
summary: John Rush explains why he chose bootstrapping over VC for Mars X, how he scouted and acquired Unicorn Platform, and why the small-acquisition market will grow. He also covers building with AI early and where AI opportunities sit: UX in boring niches, not deep tech.

principles.text: Don't build a product the big platforms will ship as a feature; go to niches Google or Gmail will ignore, like bakeries.
principles.quote: do not build a product 4G for for the email right like yeah Gmail will come with that

principles.text: The biggest AI opportunity is UX on top of models, not deep tech, which needs too many resources.
principles.quote: I would just not recommend anyone to do anything deep tech there because that's just too complicated uh and you need resources but ux is easier

principles.text: Thin AI wrappers in unexpected niches can reach $5-10k MRR; ignore the 'wrapper' criticism.
principles.quote: some people could say it's a wrapper but who cares and then they're making like you know five or ten thousand dollars a month

principles.text: Distribution used to be easy because few people built startups; now builders and marketers are rarely the same person, which fuels acquisitions.
principles.quote: it's really hard to find people who are good at both distribution and building

principles.text: Before acquiring, research the target founder obsessively; he followed Alex for a year and a half to understand what he wanted and struggled with.
principles.quote: I followed Alex for one year so I follow him for even a year and a half he didn't even know that

principles.text: Declined VC to keep the community co-ownership vision; VC funding would have harmed the project.
principles.quote: I realized that if we have VC funded company uh we can't execute on the vision of uh sharing uh you know the whole project with everyone
